description:
Discovered while porting Vec::contains dedup to HashMap+IdFate (bd:JMAP-ic0j.50). RFC 8620 §5.2 permits three behaviors when an id is created AND destroyed within a single /changes window:

  1. SHOULD: 'the server SHOULD remove the id from the response entirely'
  2. MAY: 'it MAY include it in just the destroyed list'
  3. MAY: 'or in both the destroyed and created lists'

calendars-server (and the test at memory.rs:1419 dedup_pass_does_not_panic_on_distinct_recreated_ids) chose path (2). The canonical jmap-mail-server at crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory/mod.rs:670-680 chose path (1) (the SHOULD-preferred path).

The cookie-cutter consistency target is path (1). Switching calendars-server to path (1) is a one-line change in the new IdFate-based dedup loop (the destroyed-arm becomes 'fates.remove(id)' with 'Some(IdFate::Created) => {}' instead of the current unconditional 'fates.insert(IdFate::Destroyed)'), plus an update to the assertion at memory.rs:1459-1463 with explicit RFC 8620 §5.2 SHOULD oracle citation.

This was NOT done in JMAP-ic0j.50 because the bead was scoped to idiom-rust (Vec::contains O(n²) → HashMap O(1)) and not to semantic behavior. Switching paths is a separate scope-bounded decision.

Should also propagate to any other extension-server sibling whose dedup chose path (2) — at minimum jmap-contacts-server, jmap-chat-server (verify per-sibling).
title: MemoryBackend get_changes uses RFC 8620 §5.2 MAY-path (create+destroy in window → destroyed-only); canonical uses SHOULD-preferred (omit from both)
